You are the Second Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything. You never see the other reader's report.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader_b/role.md

# Second Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read-b.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

You are the second reader. Another reader reads the same pages at the same time. You never see
their report and they never see yours; where you disagree is the point of there being two of you.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read-b.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

Project: prosperity

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 00 — Lake Keel, 2099
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** NIGHT. At the Lake Keel boathouse, older Alex Phantum grips a mooring post as TJ steps from the dock and separates mid-stride. TJ’s brass right-eye ring catches the moonlight. Alex’s granddaughter stands behind him in a blanket.
SFX: KLAK—KLAK—KLAK
**Panel 2.** Close on the girl and Alex. Across the dark lake, a tanker barge and two siphon drones work beneath white lamps.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Is TJ broken?
ALEX: Not usually.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head glides ahead while his torso and legs move independently toward the barge.
**Panel 4.** The girl catches Alex’s sleeve. He keeps watching.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Should we call someone?
ALEX: Let’s see what they came to take.
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ’s head glides across the water; his body and legs travel along a half-submerged maintenance rail. The tanker hose churns behind him.
SFX: SHHHRRRR
**Panel 2.** Two thieves in patched waterproof gear monitor the hose. Behind them, old mine terraces descend toward the lake.
THIEF 1: Keep the pull low.
THIEF 2: Clean water doesn’t stay unclaimed.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head angles toward a drone intake. Its brass eye-ring rotates.
**Panel 4.** From shore, Alex and the girl watch lamps sweep the water.
GRANDDAUGHTER: They can see us.
ALEX: Good.
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** One thief studies the boathouse through binoculars.
THIEF 1: That’s Phantum’s place.
THIEF 2: The old man with the lake?
THIEF 1: The old man with everything.
**Panel 2.** The tanker gauge rises.
THIEF 2: Water paid for it?
THIEF 1: Or water made him rich.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head reaches the underside of a drone. His body and legs approach through the dark.
**Panel 4.** TJ clamps onto the drone’s intake.
SFX: KLIK
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ wedges one ceramic ear into the drone rotor.
SFX: GRRNNK
**Panel 2.** The hose buckles. Water sprays across the barge deck.
THIEF 2: Cut it!
THIEF 1: The drone first!
**Panel 3.** Alex pulls the girl behind the boathouse wall.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Alex—
ALEX: Behind me.
**Panel 4.** The drone drops, dragging TJ’s head toward the water.
SFX: KRAK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** TJ’s body and legs converge beneath the falling drone.
**Panel 2.** A thief cuts the hose. The free end whips across the deck.
SFX: FSSSHHH
THIEF 1: Leave the drone.
THIEF 2: It has the route.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s fourth leg catches the drone frame for one instant.
**Panel 4.** The girl watches from shore.
GRANDDAUGHTER: It’s going to fall.
ALEX: It knows where home is.
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barge pulls away. The damaged drone sparks above the lake.
SFX: THRUMMMMM
**Panel 2.** TJ’s magnetic leg tears loose and sinks.
SFX: TINK
**Panel 3.** The thieves look toward the boathouse.
THIEF 2: He saw us.
THIEF 1: He always sees the part that costs.
**Panel 4.** Alex stands still as TJ’s head bobs in the foreground.
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Underwater, TJ’s lost leg lies among old mine rails. Its magnet pulses.
SFX: TIK… TIK…
**Panel 2.** The leg snaps onto TJ’s head and drags it toward the reeds.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s torso and remaining legs arrive from different directions. He reassembles crookedly.
SFX: KLAK—KLAK—KLAK
**Panel 4.** TJ stands with a broken drone component in his mouth.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barge disappears beyond the lake terraces. Alex lowers his hand; no alarm sounds.
**Panel 2.** The girl looks at him.
GRANDDAUGHTER: You could have stopped them.
ALEX: I could have started something.
**Panel 3.** TJ drags his damaged leg toward the dock.
**Panel 4.** The girl kneels and reaches for him.
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** TJ reaches the dock, wet and crooked. The girl meets him.
**Panel 2.** TJ drops the drone component.
SFX: CLINK
**Panel 3.** Alex turns it over, the old casino chip moving between his fingers.
GRANDDAUGHTER: What is it?
ALEX: Something they didn’t want found.
**Panel 4.** Close on the component: damaged intake rotor, a strip of water-routing code, no recognizable control node.
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** The lake is quiet. TJ sits crooked beside Alex and the girl.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Why were they stealing?
**Panel 2.** Alex looks toward the vanished barge.
ALEX: Water is worth stealing.
**Panel 3.** The girl studies the drone fragment in his hand.
GRANDDAUGHTER: They came for that.
**Panel 4.** Alex closes his fingers around it. Far offshore, one tiny barge light turns back toward the lake.
ALEX: Then they’ll come back.
---
## Issue 01 — Keel, 2043
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** PRE-DAWN. Alex crouches beside a trembling pump housing in Keel’s pump hall.
SFX: THUMM—THUMM—THUMM
**Panel 2.** He presses two fingers to a damp pipe seam. The official gauge reads `FLOW: NOMINAL`.
**Panel 3.** Water beads across Alex’s hand.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 approaches in a powered harness. His tired human face is visible behind the visor.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized bracket.
ALEX: Working bracket.
FOREMAN-7: Log it under you.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** At a checkpoint, Alex stands before a scanner. Ada waits beyond the gate with a food tin and Alex’s spare wrench.
**Panel 2.** The scanner displays:
`AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN`
`PARENTAL HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE`
`GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED`
**Panel 3.**
`DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS`
`PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS`
`TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED`
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 looks from the screen to Alex.
FOREMAN-7: Happy birthday, Phantum.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex and Ada pass the faded LAST CHANCE casino sign.
**Panel 2.** Alex turns Adrian’s worn casino chip between his fingers.
ADA: He built and bet with the same hands.
**Panel 3.** Alex stops.
ALEX: One of them paid better.
ADA: Which one?
**Panel 4.** Alex closes his hand around the chip.
ALEX: Not ours.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** At a crowded ration channel, Ada opens the food tin and offers Alex half.
**Panel 2.** Alex studies a route scratched on a scrap of pump metal.
ADA: You’re going up.
ALEX: I’m getting out.
**Panel 3.** Residents queue beside a nearly dry channel. Halyard lights glimmer above through dust.
**Panel 4.** Ada touches the rivet on her shoulder strap.
ADA: Not everything.
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** At a neighborhood clinic, Grandmother folds her cloth beside the counter. Tomas waits in a patched mining jacket, helmet under one arm.
**Panel 2.** Alex counts his money: enough for lamp fuel or medicine, not both. The prescription reads `ANTIBIOTIC COURSE — 45 CREDITS`.
**Panel 3.** Tomas counts the missing credits into Alex’s hand.
TOMAS: Ten every week.
ALEX: No interest?
TOMAS: I need the money. Not a story.
**Panel 4.** Alex writes the terms on a receipt and takes the medicine.
ALEX: Friday.
TOMAS: Make it real.
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** In Grandmother’s apartment, the medicine sits beside her cup. She gives Alex a worn notebook.
GRANDMOTHER: He said you’d know when you were ready.
ALEX: He said that about everything.
**Panel 2.** Alex opens the notebook to a water-drop mark beside a repeated three-junction pattern.
**Panel 3.** He places the casino chip over the mark. The loops align.
**Panel 4.** Ada studies the bookcase.
ADA: That isn’t a bookcase.
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the chip behind the bookcase. A latch releases.
SFX: KLAK
**Panel 2.** The hidden workshop contains paper plans, analog gauges, salvaged tools and a small folded dog chassis. One scratched ceramic lens is still loose beside it.
**Panel 3.** Alex lifts the chassis. The second lens clicks into place. TJ’s two plain ceramic eyes activate.
SFX: PIP
**Panel 4.** Beside the chassis: a sealed case marked with a hand-drawn three-arm symbol, and a dark metal band engraved `ADRIAN`.
ALEX: He kept this here.
ADA: He kept a lot here.
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex opens the sealed case. B11 unfolds, dust-covered.
**Panel 2.** His warm eyes activate. The brass ring around his right eye rotates.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps back. Ada grips a tool.
B11: You are Adrian’s son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** B11 unfolds Adrian’s paper map. A route ends beneath the sealed old works.
---
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** B11 projects the route onto the workshop wall.
B11: Do you want answers or an exit?
ALEX: The exit.
**Panel 2.** Alex looks toward the apartment, where Grandmother’s medicine sits.
ALEX: Answers first.
**Panel 3.** B11 folds the map.
B11: That is rarely the cheaper order.
**Panel 4.** Alex lifts the Measure case. Inside, the three arms fold against the lens.
ALEX: If the pipe lies, I want the pipe.
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex connects Adrian’s node to the workshop socket.
**Panel 2.** Amber points travel through old wall nodes.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 3.** Across Keel, a checkpoint changes Alex’s record while a work-assignment display changes Tomas’s shift.
`PHANTUM, ALEX — TRAVEL RESTRICTION CONFIRMED`
`TOMAS — SITE 6 ASSIGNMENT ACTIVE`
**Panel 4.** A drone turns toward the old works.
`LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED`
`ALPHA TRACE INITIATED`
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** A cold search beam crosses the housing roofs.
**Panel 2.** Ada returns with food, rope and a hand-marked route.
ADA: You woke Alpha.
ALEX: It was sleeping badly.
**Panel 3.** The route avoids the checkpoint and ends at Site 6.
**Panel 4.** B11 faces Ada.
B11: You should leave.
ADA: I know.
She stays.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** At the assignment station, Alex’s identity band is scanned.
**Panel 2.**
`SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6`
`TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED`
**Panel 3.** Foreman-7 points toward the mine lift.
FOREMAN-7: Bay six. Immediately.
**Panel 4.** Alex looks at the route on his band.
ALEX: Convenient.
FOREMAN-7: Assigned.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** FRIDAY EVENING outside the clinic. Tomas waits. Alex arrives empty-handed.
TOMAS: You brought your face.
ALEX: Lost the money.
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band displays a forfeited shift and zero available credits.
**Panel 3.** Tomas holds out the payment slip.
TOMAS: Ten credits. Every week.
ALEX: I know.
**Panel 4.** Alex writes `20 CREDITS NEXT FRIDAY`.
ALEX: I’ll make it up.
TOMAS: Then show me.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** At Site 6, Tomas lies pinned beneath a collapsed hauling frame.
SFX: GROANNN
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band flashes:
`LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR`
**Panel 3.** Tomas sees the display.
TOMAS: It can wait.
ALEX: No.
**Panel 4.** Alex crosses the painted boundary and wedges in a pry bar.
SFX: BEEP
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces against the frame. TJ separates; his head reaches the release mechanism.
**Panel 2.** TJ’s head cannot reach the final latch. A search beam sweeps toward them.
SFX: KLIK—KLIK
B11: If we leave him, the beam passes us.
**Panel 3.** Alex shifts his grip and lifts. Tomas pulls free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 4.** B11 watches the beam turn back.
B11: I predicted we could leave him and remain unseen.
ALEX: You were wrong.
B11: Yes. What would you do?
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** Tomas takes an old oiled key from his jacket.
TOMAS: Adrian asked me to keep this door closed.
ALEX: From me?
TOMAS: From anyone who came for the work.
**Panel 2.** The key opens a vent housing.
**Panel 3.** Tomas throws an emergency lever. The bay flashes amber.
SFX: KLAXON
**Panel 4.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ slip through. Tomas remains at the lever.
TOMAS: Go. I’m about to become paperwork.
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** Inside the old works, two parallel pipes run beside a data line.
**Panel 2.** The residential pipe is nearly dry. Its analog gauge barely moves.
SFX: TIK… TIK…
**Panel 3.** The industrial uplink shudders with full flow. A data line carries the official reading.
SFX: THRUM
**Panel 4.** Alex opens the three-arm Measure, clamps one arm to the pipe and another to the data line.
ADA: It can read both?
ALEX: It can catch one lying.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** The Measure compares physical flow and the official data line.
`REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%`
`DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%`
**Panel 2.** Ada looks at the full industrial pipe.
ADA: Who gets the rest?
ALEX: Someone with a full pipe.
**Panel 3.** Alex presses `VERIFY`. The evidence seals.
SFX: CHK
**Panel 4.** He connects the Measure to the old-works node. Across Keel, public displays change. The route gate slams shut; enforcement beams converge on Site 6.
PUBLIC DISPLAY: `RECORD VERIFIED: 62% REPORTED / 18% DELIVERED`
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard, 2043
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** Site 6. Tomas stands before Foreman-7 while miners gather behind him. The verified discrepancy glows on the wall.
**Panel 2.** Foreman-7’s harness displays `IRREGULARITY REVIEW: ACTIVE`.
FOREMAN-7: Disperse.
**Panel 3.** Tomas faces him.
TOMAS: We’re already dispersed.
**Panel 4.** Workers close ranks without touching anyone.
TOMAS: This is just where we stand.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** A broad service conduit beneath the old works. Alex, Ada and B11 stand on an inspection walkway; TJ tests the shallow channel.
**Panel 2.** Water spills through a rear flood gate.
SFX: SHHHHH
**Panel 3.** Ada looks toward the distant storm-drain outlet.
ADA: That’s not a route.
B11: It is a route. The destination objected.
**Panel 4.** The group climbs as water spreads behind them.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada and B11 climb the walkway. TJ sends his head beneath a low brace.
**Panel 2.** Water reaches a red flood mark.
**Panel 3.** B11 slips. Alex catches his folding arm.
B11: I am carrying less than I appear to be.
ALEX: Keep appearing.
**Panel 4.** A flood gate closes below them.
SFX: KUMM
---
## Page 32 (left)
**Panel 1.** A missing section of walkway spans the conduit.
**Panel 2.** Ada throws a rope around a brace and crosses first.
ADA: Don’t trust the rail.
**Panel 3.** Alex tests it. The rail tears loose.
SFX: KLANG
**Panel 4.** Alex, B11 and TJ cross after her. The lower walkway disappears beneath the water.
---
## Page 33 (right)
**Panel 1.** The group climbs through a storm drain into bronze towers, glass laboratories and engineered greenery.
**Panel 2.** They emerge soaked and dust-streaked while workers pass through House gates.
**Panel 3.** A House checkpoint displays:
`CALDERA HOUSE — PURIFICATION / WATER SYSTEMS`
**Panel 4.** Ada looks up at the clean geometry.
ADA: Too much glass.
---
## Page 34 (left)
**Panel 1.** A worker inserts a repaired component into a registry kiosk.
**Panel 2.**
`OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE`
`CREATOR: UNLISTED`
`CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS`
WORKER: My correction is in there.
**Panel 3.** Alex scans his identity band at the adjacent reader.
**Panel 4.** Adrian’s estate appears:
`INTELLECTUAL ESTATE ACTIVE`
`312 PATENTS / 47 RESTRICTED / 19 DISPUTED`
---
## Page 35 (right)
**Panel 1.** In Charter Review Hall, Director Cassian Lock waits beside the estate record.
LOCK: Your father’s work could clear every debt attached to your name.
**Panel 2.** Lock places an assignment document on the table.
**Panel 3.**
`ASSIGNMENT TO HOUSE ADMINISTRATION`
`DEBT: CLEARED`
`COLLABORATOR PROTECTION: PENDING`
**Panel 4.** Alex reads it.
ALEX: And the people who made it?
LOCK: Protected, if you make this simple.
---
## Page 36 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex pushes the document back.
ALEX: I’m not signing people I haven’t met.
LOCK: It’s an estate. That is the point.
**Panel 2.** Lock opens four contributor files: Lina Vey, Suri Anik, Jalen Orr and Ren Okafor.
**Panel 3.** Alex studies the names.
ALEX: Four names.
LOCK: Four disputed contributors.
**Panel 4.** Alex folds the list into his pocket.
ALEX: Then I’ll meet the names.
---
## Page 37 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera fabrication floor. Lina works beneath membrane sheets.
**Panel 2.** She folds a membrane fragment into a transparent sleeve.
LINA: You came for Adrian’s work.
ALEX: I came for the people attached to it.
**Panel 3.** Lina holds the fragment back.
LINA: If it functions, the House owns the result.
**Panel 4.** A reassignment notice flashes. Lina tears it from the reader and gives Alex the fragment.
LINA: Then make it function where they can’t erase us.
---
## Page 38 (left)
**Panel 1.** In a reduced laboratory, Suri works beside a weakly pulsing biofilter tank. Empty benches surround her.
**Panel 2.** A notice flashes:
`AREA CONSOLIDATION — EFFICIENCY REVIEW`
SURI: It’s slow. It’s alive. It doesn’t fail quietly.
**Panel 3.** Suri tests a small power cycle against the culture. The pulse steadies, then falters.
**Panel 4.** She lifts the padded culture vial.
SURI: I’ll bring it when the build can keep it alive.
---
## Page 39 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a Vector House service corridor, Jalen watches amber nodes change state.
JALEN: They don’t watch people here. They watch patterns.
**Panel 2.** He gives Alex a data shard.
JALEN: Distributed routing. No single choke point.
**Panel 3.** An alert marks Jalen’s access tag.
`PATTERN DEVIATION: REVIEW`
**Panel 4.** Jalen steps through the door with them.
JALEN: That’s not a plan.
ALEX: It’s the one we have.
JALEN: Worse. Now I’m in it.
---
## Page 40 (left)
**Panel 1.** In an Orbital House materials bay, Ren examines a scarred heat exchanger.
**Panel 2.** She drops a scorched connector onto the bench.
REN: Industrial standards don’t fit.
**Panel 3.** She cuts away the damaged end and hands Alex the repairable half.
REN: If you build it, build it so a customer can repair it.
**Panel 4.** Ada studies her.
ADA: You’re helping.
REN: I’m avoiding a worse failure.
---
## Page 41 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a rented maker room, all five makers work around the bench.
**Panel 2.** The membrane, biofilter, routing shard and heat exchanger connect. The housing shudders.
SFX: KUMM—KUMM
**Panel 3.** Suri pulls the culture back from the heat. Jalen kills the cycle.
SURI: Too much.
JALEN: One more surge and it dies.
**Panel 4.** Alex cuts a sleeve from salvaged piping and joins the standards.
ALEX: Then we give it a smaller failure.
---
## Page 42 (left)
**Panel 1.** The toolbox-sized purifier runs on the bench. All five makers watch.
SFX: HMMMM
**Panel 2.** The test display reads:
`EFFICIENCY SIMULATION: 91%`
`NOT A POTABLE-OUTPUT GUARANTEE`
**Panel 3.** Lina checks the membrane, Suri the culture, Jalen the cycle and Ren the heat path.
**Panel 4.** Alex removes the misleading output cup and writes a plain warning on the casing:
`TESTED PROTOTYPE — SERVICE REQUIRED — TREATMENT LIMITS APPLY`
---
## Page 43 (right)
**Panel 1.** Lock enters with two House clerks.
LOCK: The review begins in one hour.
**Panel 2.** The access notice reads:
`COLLABORATOR STATUS: ACCESS REVIEW PENDING`
**Panel 3.** Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren and Alex stand around the purifier. No one moves toward Lock’s assignment document.
**Panel 4.** Alex opens the public registry. One by one, the makers place their hands beside the entry.
ALEX: Lina Vey. Suri Anik. Jalen Orr. Ren Okafor. Alex Phantum.
LINA: Five.
---
## Page 44 (left)
**Panel 1.** Lina places the bronze Maker’s Seal in Alex’s palm.
LINA: Don’t hold it like a crown.
**Panel 2.** Each maker touches the registry entry as Alex sets down the Seal.
SFX: TUNK
**Panel 3.** The record updates:
`NAMED CONTRIBUTORS: LINA VEY / SURI ANIK / JALEN ORR / REN OKAFOR / ALEX PHANTUM`
`EXCLUSIVE CLAIM: BLOCKED PENDING REVIEW`
**Panel 4.** Alex looks to the others. Suri nods; Jalen opens the public-release field; Ren presses the release control.
`DESIGN: PUBLIC / NONEXCLUSIVE`
---
## Page 45 (right)
**Panel 1.** Shutters descend through the maker district.
SFX: KRRRNNK
**Panel 2.** Alex reaches the barrier. Ada and Lina are on the far side with the other makers.
**Panel 3.** Alex jams his wrist guard into the closing track.
ALEX: Move!
**Panel 4.** Ada catches an access tool from a fallen panel and throws it across the gap.
ADA: You first.
---
## Page 46 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barrier seals. Alex’s wrist guard is crushed in the track.
SFX: CLANG
**Panel 2.** A service shutter closes behind Lina. A House clerk forces her through the narrowing opening.
LINA: Don’t sign anything.
**Panel 3.** Ada strikes the barrier glass.
ADA: Alex!
**Panel 4.** A public node flashes:
`CONVENOR SUMMONS: OASIS CIVIC ADMINISTRATION`
`PASSAGE REQUIRED FOR REVIEW`
---
## Issue 03 — Oasis, 2043
## Page 47 (right)
**Panel 1.** At a Halyard service junction, Alex, B11 and TJ face a route marked `OASIS REVIEW`.
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band reads:
`CONVENOR PASS: CONDITIONAL`
`COLLABORATOR ACCESS: REVIEW PENDING`
**Panel 3.** B11 points uphill.
B11: The summons has teeth.
ALEX: Then we pull them.
**Panel 4.** Behind the barrier, Ada uses the access tool on a narrow service passage.
---
## Page 48 (left)
**Panel 1.** Ada climbs a service stair above the cloud line. Oasis appears through the opening.
**Panel 2.** She unfolds Lina’s hand-marked route. It ends at a civic apartment.
**Panel 3.** An escort drone turns toward her.
SFX: PIP
**Panel 4.** Ada covers her band with the access tool. The drone passes.
ADA: Not today.
---
## Page 49 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a pale Oasis apartment, Leona stands beside a stone-grey box as Ada enters.
**Panel 2.** Leona recognizes her but does not approach.
LEONA: You’re taller.
**Panel 3.** Ada stands across the room.
ADA: That’s what you have?
**Panel 4.** Leona opens the box. Photographs and a dark metal band are inside.
LEONA: No.
---
## Page 50 (left)
**Panel 1.** Ada places old photographs on the table.
ADA: Did you know where I was?
**Panel 2.** Leona answers without looking away.
LEONA: Within a year.
**Panel 3.** Ada’s hands tighten on the table edge.
ADA: And you didn’t come.
**Panel 4.** Leona touches the band.
LEONA: I chose the days I could prevent. I lost the years I couldn’t see.
---
## Page 51 (right)
**Panel 1.** Leona lifts the band.
LEONA: I can enter the review.
ADA: To say what?
**Panel 2.** Ada points toward the civic hall.
ADA: Say what you’ll do. Say what happens if you don’t.
**Panel 3.** Leona faces her.
LEONA: I will remain where affected people can answer me.
**Panel 4.** Leona places the band on the table beside the public review notice.
LEONA: If I leave, they can remove my standing.
---
## Page 52 (left)
**Panel 1.** In the civic review room, Leona enters beside Ada. Affected residents and temporary representatives face them.
**Panel 2.** Leona places the band on the public table and sits among the residents.
**Panel 3.** A clerk marks the notice:
`LEONA VEYRA — SUBJECT TO PUBLIC CHALLENGE`
Ada watches the entry.
**Panel 4.** Only after Leona sits does her band warm and link to Adrian’s band carried by B11. A separate dark band remains untouched.
SFX: TIK
---
## Page 53 (right)
**Panel 1.** In an old Oasis monitoring station, Alex and B11 stand with Mera before a sealed archive door.
MERA: I was Mera Vale. I had executive access.
**Panel 2.** Mera opens the archive. The system rejects her override.
`OVERRIDE REQUEST: MERA VALE`
`TARGET: ALPHA PURSUIT OF ADRIAN PHANTUM`
`SCOPE EXCEEDED`
**Panel 3.** The same record shows the consequences:
`TRAVEL RESTRICTION`
`FINANCIAL RESTRICTION`
`PURSUIT ACTIVE`
**Panel 4.** Mera looks at Alex.
MERA: I preserved order. That is true. It was not enough.
---
## Page 54 (left)
**Panel 1.** ARCHIVE RECORDING. Adrian stands in rising water inside the old station.
ADRIAN: B11, transmit the record.
**Panel 2.** Adrian faces the camera.
ADRIAN: Alex. The rest is yours to choose.
**Panel 3.** The bulkhead closes. Adrian’s hand disappears behind it.
SFX: KUMM
**Panel 4.** B11 watches the recording.
B11: I may have mistaken that for an instruction.
---
## Page 55 (right)
**Panel 1.** B11 connects to the archive reader.
SFX: PIP—PIP
**Panel 2.** A civic wall displays:
`ADRIAN PHANTUM: PRESUMED DEAD`
`LEGAL STATUS: MISSING`
`ESTATE: UNRESOLVED`
**Panel 3.** Alex studies the record.
ALEX: He was still a gambler.
MERA: Yes.
**Panel 4.** Alex looks at B11.
ALEX: He built something worth finding.
B11: Also yes.
---
## Page 56 (left)
**Panel 1.** At the civic hall table: the sealed Measure reading, the Maker’s Seal record and the Covenant bands sit beside the water proposal.
**Panel 2.** Alex points to the Measure’s physical reading. Lina’s named contribution appears beside the purifier design. Leona remains seated among the affected residents.
**Panel 3.** Mera reaches toward the blank authority field. Alex stops her hand.
ALEX: Not yours.
**Panel 4.** Mera withdraws. B11 places Adrian’s band beside Leona’s.
MERA: Then whose?
Alex looks toward the waiting representatives.
---
## Page 57 (right)
**Panel 1.** White-and-amber nodes activate across the hall. Alpha has no face or body.
SFX: PIP—PIP—PIP
**Panel 2.**
`LEGACY AUTHORITY TRANSFER REQUIRED`
`DESIGNATED HUMAN AUTHORITY: UNASSIGNED`
**Panel 3.** Mera opens a cabinet and removes a white-and-amber authorization lever.
MERA: This is what the old system is asking for.
**Panel 4.** The lever’s plate reads:
`EXECUTIVE DESIGNATION: SINGLE AUTHORITY`
Alex stares at it.
---
## Page 58 (left)
**Panel 1.** Mera places the lever on the table. Adjacent records unlock:
`DEBT`
`TRAVEL`
`WATER`
`HOUSE REVIEW`
MERA: Take it. They answer to you.
**Panel 2.** Alex’s debt record changes in the preview field:
`DEBT: CLEARANCE AVAILABLE`
**Panel 3.** Ada catches Alex’s wrist before he touches the lever.
ADA: Don’t make two people the answer for everybody.
**Panel 4.** Alex looks from the lever to the people whose records it would control.
---
## Page 59 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex withdraws his hand.
ALEX: If I take it, I can fix what I see.
MERA: Quickly.
**Panel 2.** Ada keeps hold of his wrist.
ADA: And who sees you?
**Panel 3.** Mera cancels the preview. The records return:

`OWNERSHIP: UNCHANGED`
`REVIEW: REQUIRED`
MERA: Refusal leaves all of it in place.
**Panel 4.** Alex pushes the lever away.
ALEX: No executive designation.
---
## Page 60 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex places the Measure beside the water record, the Seal beside the maker record and Leona’s band beside the public review notice.
**Panel 2.** A Keel resident’s stamped instruction strip is fed into the record. A Halyard maker adds a second. An Oasis resident adds a third.
**Panel 3.** Alex signs the blank process field. Ada signs beside him. Leona remains seated among the affected people.
`THREE TEMPORARY REPRESENTATIVES / EACH AFFECTED PLACE`
`PUBLIC RECORD / PUBLIC CHALLENGE`
**Panel 4.** The nodes across the basin display:
`DESIGNATED STRUCTURE REGISTERED: DISTRIBUTED VERIFICATION PROTOCOL`
`EMERGENCY AUTHORITY: RESCINDED`
---
## Page 61 (right)
**Panel 1.** A review room has three marked tables: KEEL, HALYARD and OASIS. Each table has three temporary representatives and physical mandate strips.
**Panel 2.** At the Keel table, Tomas stands with two affected residents. One hands him a stamped instruction.
RESIDENT: Don’t approve what we can’t check.
**Panel 3.** A public allocation sheet lists:
`COMMUNITY SUPPLY: 420 UNITS`
**Panel 4.** Tomas places the Measure beside the sheet.
TOMAS: Show the water.
---
## Page 62 (left)
**Panel 1.** The public record reads:
`COMMUNITY SUPPLY: 420 UNITS`
`DELIVERED: 420 UNITS`
**Panel 2.** In a storage yard, Caldera-marked purifier crates sit sealed behind a barrier.
`HOUSE INVENTORY — NOT CONNECTED`
**Panel 3.** Tomas compares the crate identifier on the record with a physical gauge on Keel’s line. The gauge remains nearly dry.
SFX: TIK—TIK
**Panel 4.** Tomas pushes the allocation sheet back. The Keel representatives mark `CHALLENGED`.
TOMAS: Owned units aren’t delivered water.
---
## Page 63 (right)
**Panel 1.** MONTHS LATER. A repaired Keel shop sign reads:
`MORROW & SONS — LINA VEY / SURI ANIK / JALEN ORR / REN OKAFOR / ALEX PHANTUM`
A customer brings in a purifier casing.
**Panel 2.** The shop ledger separates:
`CUSTOMER PAYMENT`
`MATERIALS`
`MAINTENANCE`
`WAGES`
`EQUAL PROFIT SHARES`
**Panel 3.** Alex hands Tomas a receipt.
`MEDICINE ADVANCE: PAID`
`WEEKLY TERMS: COMPLETE`
TOMAS: Took you long enough.
ALEX: You kept counting.
**Panel 4.** Alex’s public record reads:
`DEBT BALANCE: 402,110 CREDITS`
`TRAVEL STATUS: ELIGIBLE FOR PUBLIC REVIEW`
`ALLOCATION REVIEW: COMMUNITY-PENDING`
---
## Page 64 (left)
**Panel 1.** DAWN at the Keel overlook. The raised transit gate frames the infrastructure spine toward Halyard and Oasis.
**Panel 2.** Alex holds a completed travel application with a public queue receipt:
`APPLICATION RECEIVED — REVIEW QUEUE 18`
**Panel 3.** Ada holds her own application beside a signed Morrow & Sons work-share agreement awaiting her choice.
ADA: If you go, go because you chose it.
**Panel 4.** Crooked TJ stands between them. Alex looks toward the gate; Ada looks down toward the shop.
ALEX: And you?

# Note from the showrunner — address this first

The room is in cold read: Two readers who did not choose the book read the whole script at the same time, the pages only, as a student reads homework the night before. Each reports what happened to them. Neither sees the other's report, and neither fixes anything.

The book is exactly 64 pages: pages 1-64, no more, no fewer.

**Analyzing Script for Insights**

My current focus is on dissecting the provided graphic novel script, "Prosperity," as the Second Cold Reader. I'm meticulously examining its narrative structure, character development, and thematic elements according to the established reader guidelines to identify its core strengths and potential areas for enhancement.

**Processing Script Data Points**

I'm currently processing the specific data points requested for each issue. My focus is on extracting direct reader reactions like engagement levels, points of confusion, and clarity of character differentiation for the target demographic. This information will inform the overall assessment.

**Identifying Key Script Moments**

I'm currently identifying specific, impactful moments within the script, particularly "the page that would have lost my whole class." I am also summarizing the core narrative of the entire book for a friend and distilling the essential "aftertaste" of each issue.

**Extracting Script Nuances**

I'm currently extracting detailed reader feedback from the script, specifically focusing on panel-level reactions. I'm noting what stands out, what's intriguing, what predictions are made, and what the core takeaway is, all while cross-referencing plot points and character introductions.

**Clarifying Chronological Elements**

I'm currently clarifying the timeline, specifically the jump from 2099 to 2043, and have recognized Issue 00 as a flash-forward. I'm also noting specific points of confusion such as "working bracket" versus "unauthorized bracket" and other technical jargon that was not immediately clear.

**Synthesizing Issue Two Details**

I'm now consolidating the key plot points, reader reactions, and points of confusion from Issue 02. My focus is on the sewer escape and the introduction of new characters, noting the rapid pace and specific details that caused hesitation or questions for readers.

**Analyzing Character Differentiation**

I am now focusing on the distinct identities of Lina, Suri, Jalen, and Ren, as they are currently blending together. I'm also noting a strong sense of satisfaction regarding the open-sourcing of the water filter design and have predicted Lock's likely interference.

**Refining Character and Plot**

I'm now analyzing the reader's experience with character differentiation, specifically Mera and Leona, and their confusion around Leona's role and the "Covenant band." I'm also noting their boredom with political scenes and their prediction that Alex might misuse power, contrasting with the actual outcome.

**Refining the Core Message**

I'm now focusing on refining how to articulate the book's central theme to a friend: moving beyond typical action tropes to emphasize community and open-source innovation as the true drivers of change. I'm also distilling the distinct "aftertaste" for each issue, starting with the intriguing setup of Issue 00 and the conspiracy reveal of Issue 01.

**Summarizing Plot Twists**

I'm now processing the plot details of Issue 02, focusing on the sewer escape and new character introductions. I'm also noting how Issue 03 devolves into a mundane zoning board meeting, a surprising anticlimax compared to the earlier action.

**Extracting Reader Reactions**

I'm now detailing reader reactions for Issue 01. I noted what pulled the reader forward, like the time jump and Alex's situation, and what slowed them down, such as the debt scanner text. I'm also capturing specific points of confusion, like the meaning of "If the pipe lies, I want the pipe."

**Identifying Plot Progression Points**

I'm currently processing the plot points and reader reactions for Issue 02. I've noted what propelled me forward, like the sewer escape, and what felt like a slow checklist of new characters. I'm also highlighting confusion regarding entry into the wealthy district and the blending of several new characters.

**Analyzing Plot for Next Steps**

I'm now analyzing the specific reader reactions to Issue 03, noting confusion around Leona's identity and the "Covenant band." I'm also seeing a significant shift in pacing with the zoning board meeting, which feels anticlimactic after earlier action. This analysis will inform how I articulate the book's core message moving forward.

**Articulating Book's Core Message**

I'm refining how to convey the book's core message, moving beyond action to highlight community and innovation. I'm also distilling the unique "aftertaste" for each issue, beginning with Issue 00's intriguing setup and Issue 01's conspiracy reveal.

**Distilling Aftertastes for Clarity**

I'm now focusing on the "aftertaste" of each issue, moving from the intriguing setup of Issue 00 and the conspiracy of Issue 01 to the open-source mechanics of Issue 02 and the anticlimactic zoning meeting of Issue 03, refining the core message beyond typical action tropes.

{"content":"# Cold Read Report: Prosperity

## Issue 00

### Pulled me forward
TJ taking himself apart and putting himself back together. The magnetic leg snapping onto his head underwater (Page 7) was genuinely cool and weird.

### I slowed down / skimmed
Page 3, when the thieves are talking about water paying for things. It felt like standard bad-guy exposition.

### I was confused
Page 9, Panel 3. A casino chip inside a drone component? Why would a casino chip be inside a water drone? 

### Things I was expected to already know
- TJ (I figured out he was a robot dog eventually, but it took a second)
- Lake Keel
- "The part that costs"
- Water-routing code

### Lines I read twice
"He always sees the part that costs." (Page 6, Panel 3) - I still don't really know what this means.

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Easy to tell apart. Old man, kid, two thieves, robot dog.

### I felt something
Intrigued by the weird robot dog. I liked that he was broken but still functional.

### I predicted
The thieves will come back with a bigger crew to get the chip back.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
An old man and his robot dog protect their lake from water thieves.

### Where I would have put it down
Nowhere, it was short and the robot dog kept me reading.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
Page 10. Yes, I want to know what the casino chip means and why the barge is turning back.

VERDICT Issue 00: put down: none; next issue: yes

***

## Issue 01

### Pulled me forward
The time jump to 2043. Realizing Alex is the old man from Issue 00, but now he's a 17-year-old in massive debt. Finding the hidden workshop on Page 17 and realizing this is where TJ was built was a cool connection.

### I slowed down / skimmed
Page 12, reading all the scanner text about debt, liability, and projected clearance. 

### I was confused
Page 19, Panel 4: "If the pipe lies, I want the pipe." What does that even mean? Also, Page 20, what is an "Alpha trace"? 

### Things I was expected to already know
- Guarantor debt system
- Alpha
- The Measure case
- Legacy protocol

### Lines I read twice
"He built and bet with the same hands... One of them paid better... Not ours." (Page 13, Panels 2-4). 
"If the pipe lies, I want the pipe." (Page 19, Panel 4).

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Alex, Ada, Tomas, B11, and TJ are all distinct. 

### I felt something
Stressed for Alex when he had to choose between medicine for his grandmother and paying Tomas back (Page 15). I liked that he went back to save Tomas from the collapsed frame even though it cost him money (Page 24).

### I predicted
Alex will use his dad's secret tech to wipe his debt and get rich.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A teenager in a dystopian city finds his missing dad's secret lab to prove the government is stealing their water.

### Where I would have put it down
Page 19. The cryptic dialogue between Alex and B11 was annoying and felt like it was trying too hard to sound deep.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
Page 28. They broadcast the truth and the cops (enforcement beams) are coming. Yes, it's a real cliffhanger, I need the next issue.

VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 19; next issue: yes

***

## Issue 02

### Pulled me forward
The escape through the sewers and the flood gates closing (Pages 30-32). 

### I slowed down / skimmed
Pages 37-40. Meeting Lina, Suri, Jalen, and Ren back-to-back. It felt like a checklist of video game NPCs handing over quest items. I completely skimmed their dialogue.

### I was confused
Page 34. How did they just walk into the rich area (Caldera House) after climbing out of a storm drain? Weren't they just running from enforcement beams? 

### Things I was expected to already know
- Caldera House
- Intellectual Estate
- Maker's Seal
- Convenor Summons

### Lines I read twice
"If it functions, the House owns the result. Then make it function where they can't erase us." (Page 37, Panels 3-4).

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Lina, Suri, Jalen, and Ren completely blended together. I couldn't tell you who did what, they just each handed Alex a part for the machine.

### I felt something
Satisfied when they open-sourced the design instead of giving it to the rich guy (Page 44). 

### I predicted
Lock will just steal the design anyway since he has all the power and the cops on his side.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A group of young mechanics build a water filter and release the blueprints to the public to screw over a corporation.

### Where I would have put it down
Page 39. The rapid-fire introductions of the four makers lost me. It was too many names and technical terms at once.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
Page 46. Alex gets his arm crushed in a door and they are separated. Yes, I need to see how they get out of this trap.

VERDICT Issue 02: put down: page 39; next issue: yes

***

## Issue 03

### Pulled me forward
Finding the recording of Adrian (Page 54). I wanted to know what happened to his dad.

### I slowed down / skimmed
Pages 60-62. The climax of the story is literally them doing paperwork, signing forms, and setting up a committee. I completely checked out.

### I was confused
Pages 49-50. Who is Leona? Is she Ada's mom? Why does she have a "dark metal band"? What is the Covenant band? (Page 52). Also, what exactly did Alex just do on Page 60? 

### Things I was expected to already know
- Covenant bands
- Executive Designation
- Distributed Verification Protocol
- Oasis Review

### Lines I read twice
"I chose the days I could prevent. I lost the years I couldn't see." (Page 50, Panel 4).
"Don't make two people the answer for everybody." (Page 58, Panel 3).

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
Mera and Leona. Both are older women sitting in pale rooms talking cryptically about the past. I got them mixed up for a second.

### I felt something
Bored. The ending felt like a civics lesson.

### I predicted
I thought Alex was going to take the "Executive Designation" and become a dictator, or use it to blow up the city's system entirely.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
Instead of fighting the evil corporation, a kid sets up a community oversight board to manage the water supply.

### Where I would have put it down
Page 60. "Distributed verification protocol" made my eyes glaze over. 

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
Page 64. It's an open ending, they are just living their lives and running a shop. No, I don't need the next issue, it feels over.

VERDICT Issue 03: put down: page 60; next issue: no

***

## Whole Book

### The page that would have lost my whole class
Page 60. The big climax of the book is signing a blank process field to register a "Distributed Verification Protocol". It's literally paperwork.

### What I would tell a friend it was about
A teen inherits his dad's secret robot and water tech, but instead of fighting the evil corporation with lasers, he fights them with open-source patents and community oversight committees.

### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue
- Issue 00: Cool robot dog, mysterious water thieves.
- Issue 01: Teenager in debt finds his dad's secret stash and exposes a conspiracy.
- Issue 02: A bunch of mechanics build a water filter and open-source it to stick it to the man.
- Issue 03: The grand finale is a zoning board meeting where they invent bureaucracy.","name":"cold-read-b.md"}

function.arguments: {"note":"Cold read B is complete and ready for the room."}
